- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤-1.0) within 5–7 days, model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 3–8% to forecast tail.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts, especially after a spike — cap forecast slope after 3–5 days of high sentiment.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment remains bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 2–5% downward correction for days 1–7 if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with sentiment reversal point, not just historical mean.
